issues.detail: The Hebrew 'בֶּן מְשֻׁלָּם' means 'son of Meshullam' (Meshullam is a personal name), but the Chinese renders it as '梅書蘭姆人的兒子' ('son of the Meshullamite'), adding a gentilic/ethnic suffix that is not in the Hebrew. This changes the meaning from a personal patronymic to an ethnic/group designation.
